title: Intrinsic finite-coefficient derived pullback preserves bounded constructibility
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite field, and let $h:S\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant ring sheaves $A_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], ordinary module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their ordinary uncompleted derived categories $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $h^*$ be the module inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], using its canonical constant-section map $h^{-1}A_T\to A_S$.

The functor $h^*$ is exact. Termwise application therefore induces a functor $D(h^*)$ on these ordinary derived categories, and for every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^q(D(h^*)K)\cong h^*\mathcal H^q(K).$$
If an $A_T$-module sheaf $F$ is constructible in the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], then $h^*F$ is constructible in the same sense. More precisely, given a witnessing finite constructible locally closed stratification $T=\coprod_a T_a$ with inclusions $i_a$, the fibre products $S_a=S\times_TT_a$ [def-pc-fibre-product] form a witnessing stratification of $S$; empty strata may be discarded, keeping at least one stratum (so for $S=\varnothing$ a single empty stratum, on which the zero sheaf is trivially locally constant, witnesses constructibility). Writing $i'_a:S_a\to S$ and $h_a:S_a\to T_a$, its restricted module is
$$i_a'^*h^*F\cong h_a^*i_a^*F.$$
Whenever $i_a^*F$ is trivialized on a pro-étale covering $\{U_{a,b}\to T_a\}$ with finite $A$-module models $M_{a,b}$, the covering $\{S_a\times_{T_a}U_{a,b}\to S_a\}$ trivializes this restricted module with the same $M_{a,b}$; in particular its geometric stalks remain finite-dimensional over $A$.

For any scheme $Y$, let $\mathcal B_A(Y)$ consist of the complexes with cohomology zero outside a finite interval and constructible in this intrinsic sense. Then $D(h^*)\mathcal B_A(T)\subseteq\mathcal B_A(S)$, with the same cohomological vanishing interval. No assumption on the characteristic, cohomological dimension, or Noetherianity of the schemes is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(5), finite discrete specialization R=A and m=0; Lemma 6.5.8(2) for the open and closed immersions used in Lemma 6.7.11. The exactness and intrinsic stratification argument is isolated from steps 2–3 of lem-sfb-finite-field-closed-support.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison] to $h$ and $A$: the specified constant-section map $c_A^h:h^{-1}A_T\to A_S$ is an isomorphism, carrying each constant scalar to itself. The geometric morphism on these small sites is the one in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The exact fixed-ring inverse image of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], with $\Lambda=A$, therefore agrees with the module pullback in the statement. Indeed, if $N=h^{-1}F$ is regarded as an $A_S$-module through $(c_A^h)^{-1}$, the comparison $N\otimes_{h^{-1}A_T}A_S\to N$ sends $n\otimes a$ to $an$, with inverse $n\mapsto n\otimes1$. These formulas are balanced and inverse locally and hence on sheaves, naturally in $F$. The transported scalar action is the same action, since both act by the given constant scalars and extend by sheafification. Thus $h^*$ is additive and exact.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functor $h^*$ between the abelian module-sheaf categories. It carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so termwise pullback induces $D(h^*)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories, computed on every representing complex without a resolution. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], whose first assertion quantifies over every object of the unbounded derived category and every integer $q$: it gives the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^q(D(h^*)K)\cong h^*\mathcal H^q(K)$. No boundedness assumption is needed for this assertion.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); cohomology identification from homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text: Fix a witnessing stratification $T=\coprod_a T_a$ for $F$. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], the actual fibre products $S_a=S\times_TT_a$, with their projection immersions $i'_a$, form a finite locally closed stratification of $S$, with underlying subsets $h^{-1}(|T_a|)$. Each of these subsets is constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], applicable to an arbitrary scheme morphism. Inverse images preserve disjointness and the covering union. Empty strata can be removed if $S$ is nonempty; there is then at least one stratum. If $S$ is empty, retain one of the originally nonempty index set of strata, now an empty fibre product, so that the required number of strata is still at least one.

source.place: Tag 054I (lemma-inverse-image-constructible); base-change stratification as in the existing blueprint lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification

proof.text: Write $h_a:S_a\to T_a$ for the other projection. The Cartesian square gives equality of scheme morphisms $h\circ i'_a=i_a\circ h_a$. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-composition] to the two sides, with the same coefficient ring $A$ and its literal canonical coefficient maps. The two composition isomorphisms give $i_a'^*h^*F\cong (h\circ i'_a)^*F=(i_a\circ h_a)^*F\cong h_a^*i_a^*F$. This is an isomorphism of the specified $A_{S_a}$-modules, rather than just of their underlying sheaves.

Put $G_a=i_a^*F$ and choose a pro-étale trivializing covering $\{U_{a,b}\to T_a\}$ from its local constancy. Let $V_{a,b}=S_a\times_{T_a}U_{a,b}$. The base-changed arrows $V_{a,b}\to S_a$ are weakly étale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and form an fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Hence they are a covering in the small pro-étale site, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The same argument applies to any specified trivializing covering in the statement, including its possibly empty members.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism); base change of coverings and weakly etale maps in the definition of the pro-etale site

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the base-change site functor for $h_a$, with source object $U_{a,b}$ and target object $V_{a,b}=u_{h_a}(U_{a,b})$. It gives $(h_a^*G_a)|_{V_{a,b}}\cong(h_{a,b})^*(G_a|_{U_{a,b}})$ on the localized ringed sites. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], these localized sites and restricted constant coefficient rings are the small pro-étale sites and constant rings of $U_{a,b}$ and $V_{a,b}$. In these identifications the localized functor is base change by $h_{a,b}:V_{a,b}\to U_{a,b}$: both send $W\to U_{a,b}$ to $S_a\times_{T_a}W\cong V_{a,b}\times_{U_{a,b}}W$. The coefficient maps agree on constant sections. If $G_a|_{U_{a,b}}\cong\underline{M_{a,b}}$, [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] now identifies its inverse image with $\underline{M_{a,b}}$ on $V_{a,b}$. Combining this with step 4 proves the asserted trivialization of $i_a'^*h^*F$ with exactly the same model $M_{a,b}$. The argument works for all module models, and in particular for the finite models specified in the statement.

For a geometric point $\bar s$ of $S_a$, put $\bar t=h_a\bar s$. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] and the identification in step 1, forgetting the scalars of $h_a^*G_a$ gives the abelian inverse image of $G_a$. Thus [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] gives an additive isomorphism $(h_a^*G_a)_{\bar s}\cong(G_a)_{\bar t}$. It is $A$-linear: naturality for the endomorphism multiplication by each $a\in A$ says exactly that the isomorphism commutes with that scalar, and the coefficient comparison fixes constant scalars. The right-hand stalk is finite by the witnessing constructibility of $F$. Consequently the left-hand stalk is finite, hence finite-dimensional over the field $A$. Together with the local trivializations of step 6, this verifies every condition of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] on the stratification of step 3. When $S=\varnothing$, every object of its site is empty; the sheaf condition for the empty covering makes all its module sections zero. Its unique module sheaf is therefore the constant zero sheaf, and the retained single empty stratum witnesses constructibility.

source.place: Tag 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites); proetale.tex Tag 0993 (lemma-classical-point); intrinsic constructibility as defined in the cited DAG node

proof.text: Finally let $K\in\mathcal B_A(T)$ and let $[a,b]$ be any finite interval outside which its cohomology vanishes. The isomorphism of step 2 identifies each cohomology sheaf of $D(h^*)K$ with the pullback of the corresponding cohomology sheaf of $K$. Steps 3–7 make this pullback constructible. For $q\notin[a,b]$ it is $h^*(0)=0$, since an additive functor preserves zero objects. Hence $D(h^*)K\in\mathcal B_A(S)$ with the same vanishing interval. All arguments used arbitrary scheme maps and ordinary constant-ring module sheaves; none required characteristic restrictions, Noetherianity or a cohomological-dimension bound.
